why.eyebrow: Built by and for QA teams
why.title: Why QA FlowKit
why.intro: AI agents can generate tests quickly, but QA teams still need structure, traceability, approval points and reproducible validation. QA FlowKit is 100% oriented to QA workflow — not app scaffolding or generic coding prompts.

cards.title: The problem
cards.text: Ad hoc prompts produce inconsistent Gherkin, lost RF links and CI with no clear contract for what “done” means in QA.

cards.title: The approach
cards.text: A repository-native QA harness: phased workflows, explicit approvals and deterministic validators — not prompt discipline alone.

cards.title: For QA workflows
cards.text: From requirement intake through Gherkin, traceability matrix, automation plan and release evidence — every step has defined outputs.

cards.title: Clear boundaries
cards.text: No bundled AI model, no telemetry, no silent external writes. Artifacts stay local and auditable inside the repository.

without.title: Without a QA harness
items: One-off prompts with no phase order
RF and acceptance criteria lost across sessions
CI has no shared quality gate for QA artifacts

with.title: With QA FlowKit
items: validate-target runs the full repository quality gate
run start | next | check resumes work across agent sessions
Proposal-first synchronization plans — no silent test-management writes

workflow.title: From requirements to release evidence
workflow.intro: The AI reasons and edits files. QA FlowKit controls phase order, required outputs, approvals and pass/fail checks so teams do not rely only on prompt discipline.

layers.title: AI agent
layers.text: Reasons about requirements, drafts Gherkin, proposes synchronization plans and automation — edits files in the repository.

layers.title: QA FlowKit harness
layers.text: Validates outputs, blocks invalid phases, records approvals and keeps resumable run state under .qa-ai/state/.

workflow.notes: Key control gates include official RF ID confirmation, proposal-first test-management synchronization, risk scoring, environment readiness checks and deterministic Gherkin validation before traceability and release decisions.
workflow.track_intro: When you install QA FlowKit, you choose how much of the QA journey it guides. New capabilities (risk analysis, test data, environments, execution, result analysis, defect triage, and learning loop) are opt-in and ship off or advisory by default.
tracks: Quick — Manual QA teams: requirements → Gherkin → traceability matrix (risk analysis optional, strategy routing off)
Standard — Full workflow with advisory risk, test data, environments and specialist routing from requirement signals
Enterprise — Full workflow plus release gate, execution evidence and learning loop

features.title: A portable QA harness for QA repositories
features.intro: QA FlowKit adds the framework folder, target repository configuration, generated artifacts, Gherkin files and optional agent adapters directly inside the repository under test.

items.title: Traceable test design
items.text: Validate RF links, duplicate IDs, coverage obligations and acceptance-criteria blocks.

items.title: Deterministic validators
items.text: Check Gherkin language, required tags, synchronization plans, release gates and generated QA artifacts.

items.title: Right-sized workflow
items.text: Start lean for manual QA or use the full path when you plan automation. Teams with audit needs can add an optional formal release checklist later.

items.title: Resumable harness
items.text: Persistent run state, append-only event log and run status across agent sessions.

items.title: On-demand specialist routing
items.text: Route privacy, mobile, security, cloud and other strategy specialists from requirement signals. Standard presets use advisory mode; strict mode can enforce documented routing decisions.

items.title: Safety boundaries
items.text: Keep outputs local, reject unsafe paths, scan untrusted content and avoid external writes in the MVP.

commands.title: CLI and agent commands
commands.intro: Run initial setup and validation from the terminal. Drive the QA flow from your AI coding tool with generated slash commands.
commands.agent_group_note: Slash commands generated under .claude/commands/ or .opencode/commands/ after init. Each card links to its command definition in the framework.

agent_commands.description: Context-aware guidance — what to do next in the QA flow.
Guided QA FlowKit initialization inside the agent session.
Run the full guided QA FlowKit flow from start to finish.
Add QA tests for a new requirement (RF).
Review and apply approved updates to existing tests after RF changes.
Classify existing .feature files and plan automation backlog.
Analyze functional coverage across RFs, manual tests and automated tests.
Propose affected tests from a branch, commit, PR or change reference.
Evaluate Gherkin quality for an RF or feature path.
Summarize config, artifacts, feature health and recommended next steps.
Run setup health checks for the framework and target repository.
Preview or execute manifest-based cleanup of generated files.
Validate QA design Gherkin files against framework rules.
Validate executable Karate features against framework rules.
Optional: formal release checklist and stricter validation for audit-sensitive teams.
Record a documented go/no-go decision when using the optional release checklist.

terminal_commands.description: Copy .qa-ai/ into the repository. Then configure with /qa-init or node .qa-ai/scripts/init.mjs.
Installation health check for the framework and target repository configuration.
Recommend the next QA flow step based on current artifacts.

terminal_commands.code: npx qa-flowkit run start | next | check
terminal_commands.description: Resumable harness with per-phase validation and approval gates.
Run the full target-repository quality gate (strict doctor + validators).
Export Gherkin-aligned test cases to Cucumber JSON, Allure or JUnit XML.
